title: Sound — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: The survey's biggest surprise. Memory said "plan, SN0 next" — the code says one of the most fully-realized planes in the library: SN0–SN6 and a sonification series shipped and closed. miniaudio is vendored and split into two DLLs, there's an owned Zig sound graph (Web-Audio-shaped), FFT-backed analysis on the shared engine FFT, and — the pro-audio correctness axis JUCE obsesses over — a real lock-free real-time callback that does no allocation, no lock, and never re-enters the Ring VM, guarded down to worst-callback microseconds. On top sits a distinctive sonification / earcon / voice layer no mainstream audio library offers. What it refuses on purpose: MIDI, spatial/HRTF, plugin hosting, notation — and reverb is absent even from the effect palette.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. Measured against miniaudio (the vendored engine), Web Audio (the graph model) and JUCE (the pro framework) — a real, well-built plane with a thin effect palette and one deliberate breadth boundary.

lanes.engine: The pro-audio correctness axis, implemented in Zig (`audiodev.zig` `sinkCallback`): the audio callback does no allocation, no lock, and never re-enters the Ring VM — an SPSC lock-free ring (`soundring.zig`, magic/version-checked, two atomics), capacity-reserved tables that never reallocate under a live callback, underruns counted, worst-callback microseconds tracked.
lanes.owed: This is the discipline serious audio frameworks are built on, and it is genuinely built and guarded — not aspired to. A real strength.

lanes.engine: `audiodev.zig` over vendored miniaudio device backends (per-OS): open / start / stop / close, a `stzSoundTransport` face, and an honest report when no device is present. Split into a portable decode DLL and a device DLL.
lanes.owed: Real cross-platform device I/O via the reference low-level library, wired with the correct callback discipline (lane 1). At parity for playback.

lanes.engine: An owned node graph (`soundgraph.zig` — miniaudio's own graph is deliberately disabled): node kinds OSC / SOURCE / GAIN / MIX / PAN / FILTER / DELAY / ENVELOPE over planar buses, topological and cycle-free, with real-time streaming (graph + ring + producer thread).
lanes.owed: The Web-Audio / JUCE graph model, built in-house — a real routing engine, not a wrapper. The node palette is where the effects gap sits (lane 11).

lanes.engine: `soundanalysis.zig` on the shared `fft.zig`: spectrum (Hann-windowed), threaded spectrogram, onset detection, tempo estimation, LUFS loudness (momentary + short-term, broadcast standard), and dominant frequency.
lanes.owed: Well beyond Web Audio's basic analyser — spectrogram, onsets, tempo and LUFS reach toward librosa territory. A genuinely rich analysis lane.

lanes.engine: A distinctive shipped layer: `stzEarcons` (66 methods), `stzVoice` / `stzVoicePool` (text→sound), `stzListener` (sound→text, closed grammar), and the SS1–SS5 sonification series (contour/timbre identity, loudness binding, ducking, a shared data-to-sound vocabulary).
lanes.owed: Turning data into meaningful sound with a governed vocabulary and ducking is something no mainstream audio library offers — a distinctive, shipped capability, consistent with the library's accessibility DNA.

lanes.engine: `sound.zig` decodes WAV / MP3 / FLAC / OGG (via miniaudio), with resample and channel conversion; encodes WAV and FLAC (`SaveWav` / `SaveFlac` / `ToWavBytes`).
lanes.owed: Decode covers the common formats; encode is WAV/FLAC only — MP3/OGG out return `UNSUPPORTED`. Read-broad, write-narrow.

lanes.engine: `sounddsp.zig` — band-limited oscillators (polyBLEP / polyBLAMP anti-aliasing) for sine / square / saw / triangle, plus an ADSR `Envelope`, all f64 and unit-tested.
lanes.owed: Correct anti-aliased oscillators + ADSR — but a modest palette: no wavetable, FM, additive or granular synthesis, and one envelope shape.

lanes.engine: Microphone capture through the same device layer and the same callback discipline (`audiodev.zig` capture side, `stzMicrophone.ring`), reporting honestly when no input device is present.
lanes.owed: Real, lock-free mic capture — solid for recording and live input. Multi-device selection and format negotiation depth are where it stays basic.

lanes.engine: Real-time streaming through the graph (`soundgraph.zig` "the stream"): a producer thread feeds the lock-free ring the callback drains, bounded at `MAX_STREAMS=16`, with `StreamStart` / `Stop` / `Drain`.
lanes.owed: Streaming from a producer to the device works and is bounded. Network streaming / adaptive buffering is not part of the lane.

lanes.engine: `stzSoundPlot` and `stzSoundGrid` render waveforms and spectrograms through the library's own graphics plane — audio analysis drawn as SVG/PNG grids, plus a browser guard harness.
lanes.owed: A distinctive convergence — the sound plane borrowing the graphics engine to show what it hears — though the visual vocabulary (waveform, spectrogram) is small next to a full DAW's meters and scopes.

lanes.engine: Correct RBJ biquad filters (lowpass / highpass / bandpass), a delay with a feedback line, gain and pan — the workhorse effects, in Zig.
lanes.owed: No reverb (absent even as a named node), and no compressor / chorus / distortion / dynamics. Filters and delay are solid; the effect palette is thin next to JUCE or the Web Audio node set.

lanes.engine: None — and stated in writing as deliberate non-goals: MIDI, music notation, 3D/HRTF spatial audio, time-stretching, and VST/CLAP plugin hosting are all "OUT until asked."
lanes.owed: The pro-framework breadth JUCE is chosen for — plugin hosting, MIDI, spatialization, time-stretch — is absent by choice. A real gap against JUCE, and a deliberate scope line, not an oversight.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first fills the obvious holes in an otherwise-real DSP; the second adds output breadth and the most-requested of the deferred features; the third is the pro-framework reach it refuses today.

tiers.title: Tier A — fill the DSP holes

items.title: Reverb & a fuller effect palette
items.text: A reverb node (absent entirely today) plus compressor, chorus and distortion over the existing graph. The routing engine and filters are real; the effect palette is the one obvious gap in an otherwise-complete DSP.

items.title: Richer synthesis
items.text: Wavetable, FM, additive and granular synthesis, and more envelope/LFO shapes, over the correct band-limited oscillator base — lifting synthesis from a modest set to an instrument.

tiers.title: Tier B — output breadth & the first deferred features

items.title: MP3 / OGG encode
items.text: Encode already covers WAV/FLAC and decode covers everything; adding lossy encode (MP3/OGG) closes the read-broad / write-narrow asymmetry so a processed clip can be saved in the format it arrived in.

items.title: MIDI input
items.text: The most-requested of the deferred set — MIDI in, to drive the synthesizer from a controller or a sequence. A natural next step once a workload asks, without reopening the whole pro-audio scope.

items.title: GPU-FFT for large offline analysis
items.text: `gpu_fft.zig` exists (measured ~13× on the iGPU); wire it for offline long-transform analysis (deliberately keeping realtime DSP on CPU/SIMD), so a full-track spectrogram is fast.

tiers.title: Tier C — the pro-framework reach (deliberate non-goals)

items.title: Spatial / 3D / HRTF audio
items.text: Positional audio and HRTF spatialization — the immersive layer Web Audio and JUCE offer. Out of scope today; a revisit-on-demand item, not an oversight.

items.title: Plugin hosting (VST / CLAP)
items.text: Hosting third-party audio plugins — the thing JUCE is chosen for. It would ride the (planned) extensibility plane's governed-foreign-capability model, and is deliberately deferred until asked.

items.title: Time-stretch & pitch-shift
items.text: Independent tempo/pitch manipulation — the last of the stated non-goals, useful for the analysis and sonification lanes as much as for playback.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings — and a memory correction.
notes.text: Re-surveyed from `main`, and the project-memory line ("Sound plane PLAN, SN0 next") is stale: SN0 was the go/no-go spike and everything through SN6 plus a sonification series SS1–SS5 shipped and closed. It is guarded by a 31-file test corpus plus a WASM / Web-Audio browser guard harness (`earcon_expect.json`, `voice_guard.html`), and the real-time callback contract (no alloc / no lock / no Ring) is implemented and guarded — SPSC ring with magic/version checks and worst-callback-microsecond tracking. The deliberate non-goals (MIDI, notation, 3D/HRTF, time-stretch, VST/CLAP) are stated in writing; reverb is absent as a named effect.

Softanza's sound is a real, correctly-built audio engine — a lock-free realtime callback, an owned Web-Audio-shaped graph, librosa-grade analysis, and a sonification layer no competitor has — that stops short of a pro DAW/host on purpose: a thin effect palette (no reverb) and the deliberate absence of MIDI, spatial audio and plugin hosting.

footer: Read from the source on 2026-09-16, from a read-only `main` worktree — Ring faces under `base/sound` (`stzSound`, `stzSoundGraph`, `stzSoundTransport`, `stzSoundPlot/Grid`, `stzEarcons`, `stzVoice/VoicePool`, `stzListener`, `stzMicrophone`); engine `sound.zig`, `soundgraph.zig`, `soundanalysis.zig`, `audiodev.zig`, `sounddsp.zig`, `soundring.zig`, `soundwasm.zig` + vendored `miniaudio 0.11.25`, reusing `fft.zig`; two DLLs (`stz_sound`, `stz_audiodev`); plans of record `SOFTANZA_SOUND_PLAN.md` (SN0–SN6, SS1–SS5) + `SOFTANZA_VOICE_PLAN.md`; guards under `test/sound` (31 files + a web-audio harness). Ratings reflect what the guards prove.
